name: Cisco ASA — Outbound SMTP Spam Bot Activity
xql_query:
datamodel dataset = cisco_asa_raw
| filter cisco_asa_raw._raw_log contains "302013"
       and xdm.target.port in (25, 587)
       and xdm.source.interface = "inside" and xdm.target.interface = "outside"
| alter sender_ip = xdm.source.ipv4
| bin _time span = 1h
| comp count_distinct(xdm.target.ipv4) as distinct_mx,
       values(xdm.target.ipv4) as mx_hosts,
       values(xdm.target.port) as mx_ports
       by sender_ip, _time
| filter distinct_mx >= 20
| fields sender_ip, mx_hosts, mx_ports, distinct_mx
description: Internal host fanning out SMTP connections to many distinct external mail destinations — spam-bot indicator.
alert_name: Cisco ASA — Outbound SMTP Spam Bot Activity
alert_description:
What fired: Internal host fanning out SMTP connections to many distinct external mail destinations — spam-bot indicator.

Why it matters: a host is communicating with known-bad or anomalous infrastructure (C2 / malicious domain). Assessed severity: High.

MITRE ATT&CK: T1071 - Application Layer Protocol (TA0011 - Command and Control).

Investigate:
  - Identify the internal client and the domain/IP contacted, and check reputation + resolution history.
  - Look for the initial delivery vector (email/web/download) and any beaconing cadence or follow-on payloads from the same host.
  - Pivot on the alert's key entity (xdm.target.ipv4) to related activity in the same window.
  - Confirm the activity is not expected/authorized for the involved entity before escalating.
